chunks: And ʿAmr ibn Khālid narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to fast Shaʿbān and the month of Ramaḍān, joining them together, and he would forbid the people from joining them together. And he used to say: “They are the two months of Allah, and they are an expiation for the sins before them and after them.”

key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of obligatory fasting in Islam.
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The month of Shaʿbān, the month preceding Ramaḍān.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: A means of expiation or atonement for sins.
key_terms.يَصِلُهُمَا: He joined the two months together in fasting without separating them.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about fasting Shaʿbān together with Ramaḍān?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would continue fasting from Shaʿbān into Ramaḍān without a break, while prohibiting others from doing the same. It also emphasizes the special sanctity of these two months and describes them as a means of expiation for sins.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1826 - Amr ibn Khalid narrates from Abu Ja‘far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) would fast Sha‘ban and the Month of Ramadan together without separating them, but he would forbid people from joining them together. He used to say: ‘They are the months of Allah (swt), and they are an expiation for the sins committed before and after them.’”
